chunks: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'How excellent are the daughters as children — kind, serving, caring, blessed, loving.'

key_terms.مُجَهِّزَاتٌ: Those who prepare/serve/provide; from جهّز (to equip, to prepare)
key_terms.مُفَلِّيَاتٌ: Devoted, loving; from فلا (to groom with affection, to care for tenderly)
key_terms.مُلْطِفَاتٌ: Kind, gentle, affectionate; from لطف (to be gentle/kind)
key_terms.مُونِسَاتٌ: Companionable, caring, comforting; from أنس (intimacy, comfort)
key_terms.نِعْمَ: Particle of highest praise in Arabic (how excellent!); used for superlative commendation

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about the virtue of daughters?
ai.summary: In this hadith, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) transmits a saying of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) praising daughters with five virtuous qualities: kindness, service, companionship, blessedness, and devotion. This tradition stands in direct contrast to the pre-Islamic Arab culture of female infanticide and the shame felt upon the birth of daughters, as condemned in the Quran (16:58-59). The Prophet's praise elevates daughters and affirms their spiritual and social worth in the household.
